newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Falling Wall Street spooks Asian markets.
newsitem.headline: Falling Wall Street spooks Asian markets.

text.p: Asian markets closed mostly lower on Friday on poor sentiment from the Wall Street's overnight fall and local factors, brokers said.
Shares in Tokyo fell sharply to end below the 21,000 point level and stocks in Manila fell 2.6 percent to 2,962.6 after heavy selling in Philippine National Bank spread to other major counters.

Elsewhere, shares in Sydney, which ended at a record high on Thursday, fell sharply in the wake of Wall Street's 44 point drop and disappointment that Australia's central Reserve Bank did not move to lower rates on Friday morning.
The Dow Jones Industrial Index ended at 5,992.48 points, its fourth consecutive lower close.

South Korean shares also ended lower, down 1.33 percent to 793.78 on an uncertain market outlook, but Singapore shares ended up 17.59 points to 2,077.2 to become one of the region's best performers of the day.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei average fell for the fifth successive day as investor sentiment was bogged down by uncertainties over a new coalition government as well as the state of the economy, brokers said.
The key benchmark of 225 selected issues shed 263.52 points, or 1.25 percent, to end at 20,739.97, closing below the 21,000 threshold for the first time in two weeks.
"There were fervent hopes for a rebound in the Nikkei average but the index showed no signs of regaining its feet," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities.
In Sydney, profit-taking erased all of Thursday's record-breaking gains after Wall Street's fall.
Options exercises, following Thursday's October series expiries, drove volumes and the vast majority of turnover put through the market was before the start of trade.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 42.4 points lower at 2,335.2, it biggest one-day fall since July 16.

"Basically, there was too much euphoric buying yesterday on comments from the prime minister that the wages data would prompt a rate cut," said Stuart Smith, senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage Lance Jones.
Hong Kong stocks closed down on profit-taking as well as Wall Street's weaker close, which heightened caution on the near term outlook for the local market, brokers said.
"After four days of declines on Wall Street, we had to expect some consolidation of the Hang Seng," said the sales director of a Japanese brokerage.
The Hang Seng Index closed 85.18 points down at 12,388.38, off a low of 12,343.27.

The dollar was at its highs in Tokyo, but its movements were tightly sandwiched between profit-taking and option-related offers and bids from Japanese importers, dealers said. The dollar traded at 113.05/15 yen and 1.5211/16 marks, compared with New York's previous close of 112.81/91 yen and 1.5175/80 marks.
At 1055 GMT, the dollar was trading at 113.37/42 yen and 1.5242/49 marks.
Bullion ended at US$382.30/382.80 an ounce in Hong Kong, against New York's previous close of US$382.85/383.25.

In Singapore, Brent December crude futures traded higher on SIMEX by late trade compared with London's settlement on Thursday. December traded at $23.86 per barrel, compared with London's settlement at $23.75.
